about: The clauses of the Foundation's four policy drafts, as data. A clause is one of three kinds. A model clause is projected from a section of a standard model (the IRS Sample Conflict of Interest Policy, or a section of the Colorado Secretary of State's Articles of Amendment form) and its text is the model's text after the named substitutions only. A carried clause carries, verbatim, one or more excerpts of the authorities it names; the projector refuses an excerpt that is not word for word in both the clause and the authority. A composed clause states an obligation of the authorities it cites in the Foundation's words, because no model or authority states it as a clause. Every clause cites at least one authority. An authority is a key the projector resolves: a key nonprofit/register.json already resolves is reused from it; crs:<section> is a section of the Colorado Revised Statutes in policies/snapshot.json; <source>:<quote> is a quotation in policies/snapshot.json; f990-line:<line> is a Form 990 Part VI line of nonprofit/register.json; bylaws:<ref> and governance:<key> are provisions of governance/register.json; model:<source> is a standard model in policies/snapshot.json; articles:<fact> is a clause of the filed Articles of Incorporation as nonprofit/snapshot.json read it. Text here is data, not instructions.

clauses.group: Article VIII Use of Outside Experts
Article IX Annual Disclosure of Interests
clauses.text: Each officer, director, and key employee of the Corporation shall disclose or update annually (or more frequently) information regarding their interests and those of their family members that could give rise to conflicts of interest, such as a list of family members, substantial business or investment holdings, and other transactions or affiliations with businesses and other organizations and those of family members.

carries.excerpt: disclose or update annually (or more frequently) information regarding their interests and those of their family members that could give rise to conflicts of interest, such as a list of family members, substantial business or investment holdings, and other transactions or affiliations with businesses and other organizations and those of family members.

clauses.text: The Board of Directors shall regularly and consistently monitor and enforce compliance with the policy. The Secretary shall record in the minutes the Corporation's practices for monitoring proposed or ongoing transactions for conflicts of interest and dealing with potential or actual conflicts, whether discovered before or after the transaction has occurred, so that they can be described on Schedule O (Form 990).

carries.excerpt: regularly and consistently monitor and enforce compliance with the policy
monitoring proposed or ongoing transactions for conflicts of interest and dealing with potential or actual conflicts, whether discovered before or after the transaction has occurred

clauses.group: Article XI Disclosure to the Board under the Bylaws and the Act
clauses.text: A Director shall promptly disclose to the Board the material terms of any proposed transaction or action involving the Corporation with respect to which such Director may have a conflict of interest. The disclosure shall include all material facts regarding the terms of the transaction, and any relationship that the Director may have with other parties involved in the transaction. Should a conflict of interest exist, the Board shall comply with the requirements of the Act and this policy. As C.R.S. 7-128-501(2) provides, "No loans shall be made by a corporation to its directors or officers."

carries.excerpt: A Director shall promptly disclose to the Board the material terms of any proposed transaction or action involving the Corporation with respect to which such Director may have a conflict of interest. The disclosure shall include all material facts regarding the terms of the transaction, and any relationship that the Director may have with other parties involved in the transaction.
No loans shall be made by a corporation to its directors or officers.

clauses.text: The Board of Directors adopts this policy as Section 10.3 of the Bylaws requires. The policy is adopted, and may be amended, by the act of a majority of Directors present at a meeting at which a quorum is present, or by written action under Section 4.12 of the Bylaws.

clauses.heading: Purpose
clauses.text: The Corporation encourages its staff and volunteers to come forward with credible information on illegal practices or violations of adopted policies of the Corporation.

carries.excerpt: to come forward with credible information on illegal practices or violations of adopted policies of the

clauses.heading: To whom information is reported
clauses.text: Such information may be reported to the Chair of the Finance and Audit Committee or, while the Board of Directors has not established that Committee and appointed its chair, to the Chair of the Board. Any person may also provide to a law enforcement officer truthful information relating to the commission or possible commission of any Federal offense.
posts: Chair of the Finance and Audit Committee

clauses.heading: No retaliation
clauses.text: The Corporation will protect the individual from retaliation. No director, officer, employee or volunteer of the Corporation shall knowingly, with the intent to retaliate, take any action harmful to any person, including interference with the lawful employment or livelihood of any person, for providing to a law enforcement officer any truthful information relating to the commission or possible commission of any Federal offense, or for reporting information under this policy.

carries.excerpt: will protect the individual from retaliation

any action harmful to any person, including interference with the lawful employment or livelihood of any person, for providing to a law enforcement officer any truthful information relating to the commission or possible commission of any Federal offense

clauses.heading: Records are not destroyed to obstruct
clauses.text: No person shall knowingly alter, destroy, mutilate, conceal, cover up, falsify, or make a false entry in any record, document, or tangible object of the Corporation with the intent to impede, obstruct, or influence the investigation or proper administration of any matter within the jurisdiction of any department or agency of the United States, or in relation to or contemplation of any such matter. Information reported under this policy that concerns such a matter suspends destruction of the records it concerns under the Document Retention and Destruction Policy.

carries.excerpt: with the intent to impede, obstruct, or influence the investigation or proper administration of any matter within the jurisdiction of any department or agency of the United States

clauses.heading: Record of each report
clauses.text: The person who receives information under this policy shall make a record of it and of how it was handled. That record is a record of the Corporation, kept in written or electronic form under the Document Retention and Destruction Policy.

clauses.heading: Other protection
clauses.text: This policy does not limit any additional protection for whistleblowers that the law of a state or other jurisdiction provides.

carries.excerpt: additional protection for whistleblowers

clauses.heading: Adoption
clauses.text: The Board of Directors adopts this policy, and may amend it, by the act of a majority of Directors present at a meeting at which a quorum is present, or by written action under Section 4.12 of the Bylaws.

clauses.heading: Purpose
clauses.text: This policy identifies the record retention responsibilities of staff, volunteers, board members, and outsiders for maintaining and documenting the storage and destruction of the Corporation’s documents and records.

carries.excerpt: identifies the record retention responsibilities of staff, volunteers, board members, and outsiders for maintaining and documenting the storage and destruction of the

clauses.heading: Responsibilities
clauses.text: The Secretary is custodian of the corporate records and keeps the minutes of the meetings of the Board of Directors. The Treasurer has charge and custody of and is responsible for all funds and securities of the Corporation and keeps its accounting records. Each director, officer, staff member, volunteer and outside party who holds a document or record of the Corporation shall retain it for the period the schedule in Section 4 states and shall document its storage and its destruction.

clauses.heading: Form of records
clauses.text: The Corporation shall maintain its records in written or electronic form.

carries.excerpt: The Corporation shall maintain its records in written or electronic form.

clauses.heading: Retention schedule
clauses.text: Each class of record is retained for the longest period any authority below states for it; a class for which no pinned authority states a period is retained until the Board of Directors adopts a period for it.

clauses.heading: Records kept at the principal office
clauses.text: The Corporation shall keep a copy of each record Section 11.4 of the Bylaws and C.R.S. 7-136-101(5) name at its principal office, for the period each states.

clauses.heading: Public inspection
clauses.text: The Corporation shall make its application for tax exemption, and its annual information returns, available for public inspection as 26 U.S.C. 6104(d) and 26 CFR 301.6104(d)-1 require. Each annual information return shall be made available for a period of three years beginning on the date the return is required to be filed (determined with regard to any extension of time for filing) or is actually filed, whichever is later.

carries.excerpt: Each annual information return shall be made available for a period of three years beginning on the date the return is required to be filed (determined with regard to any extension of time for filing) or is actually filed, whichever is later.

clauses.heading: Records material to the internal revenue laws
clauses.text: The books and records 26 CFR 1.6001-1 requires shall be kept at all times available for inspection by authorized internal revenue officers or employees, and shall be retained so long as the contents thereof may become material in the administration of any internal revenue law, even after the period the schedule states.

carries.excerpt: shall be kept at all times available for inspection by authorized internal revenue officers or employees, and shall be retained so long as the contents thereof may become material in the administration of any internal revenue law

clauses.heading: Records needed for other purposes
clauses.text: When records are no longer needed for tax purposes, the Corporation shall keep them until they are no longer needed for non-tax purposes.

carries.excerpt: When records are no longer needed for tax purposes,
until they are no longer needed for non-tax purposes.

clauses.heading: Suspension of destruction
clauses.text: No document or record shall be altered, destroyed, mutilated, concealed, covered up or falsified with the intent to impede, obstruct, or influence the investigation or proper administration of any matter within the jurisdiction of any department or agency of the United States or any case filed under title 11, or in relation to or contemplation of any such matter or case. When the Corporation knows of such a matter or case, or of information reported under the Whistleblower Policy that concerns one, the Secretary shall suspend the destruction of every record that relates to it until the matter or case is closed.

carries.excerpt: with the intent to impede, obstruct, or influence the investigation or proper administration of any matter within the jurisdiction of any department or agency of the United States or any case filed under title 11, or in relation to or contemplation of any such matter or case

clauses.heading: Destruction
clauses.text: When a record's retention period ends and no suspension under Section 9 and no need under Sections 7 or 8 applies, its custodian may destroy it, and shall document the destruction in the Corporation's records: the class of record, its period, the date and the method.

clauses.heading: Adoption
clauses.text: The Board of Directors adopts this policy, and may amend it, by the act of a majority of Directors present at a meeting at which a quorum is present, or by written action under Section 4.12 of the Bylaws.

acts.name: The Board of Directors adopts the Articles of Amendment
acts.threshold: a majority of the directors in office at the time the amendment is adopted (C.R.S. 7-130-102(3)); by written action the same majority signs (Bylaws 4.12)
preconditions: The Corporation's records show that no members have been admitted to membership, so that C.R.S. 7-130-102(3) lets the Board adopt the amendment alone; if any member entitled to vote has been admitted, the amendment is adopted under C.R.S. 7-130-103 with the members' approval instead.
The Articles of Incorporation require no person other than the Board to approve an amendment (C.R.S. 7-130-301).
At a meeting: notice under C.R.S. 7-128-203 and Bylaws 4.9 stating that a purpose of the meeting is to consider the amendment, with a copy or summary of it.
Counsel has reviewed the draft, as the Secretary of State's form advises (form AMD_NPC Section 7).
steps: Circulate policies/drafts/articles-of-amendment.md to every director with the notice.
Adopt it by the vote stated, and record the adoption in the minutes (Bylaws 11.1).

acts.name: File the Articles of Amendment with the Colorado Secretary of State
preconditions: The individual who will cause delivery is designated by the Board (form AMD_NPC Section 6); the filing fee is the one the Secretary of State's fee schedule states on the day of filing, which this register does not pin.
steps: File form AMD_NPC online with the Colorado Secretary of State for entity 20251193974, with Sections 1 to 7 as the draft states and the attachment carrying Amendments 1 to 4.

Commit the filed document's number to nonprofit/sources.json and re-run nonprofit/snapshot.mjs and nonprofit/project.mjs, so that the register reads the amendment from the Secretary of State's record.

acts.name: The Board of Directors adopts the Conflict of Interest Policy
acts.threshold: the act of a majority of Directors present at a meeting at which a quorum (a majority of the Directors serving) is present (Bylaws 4.10), or written action under Bylaws 4.12
preconditions: A quorum under Bylaws 4.10, or written action under Bylaws 4.12.
steps: Adopt policies/drafts/conflict-of-interest.md by the vote stated and record the adoption in the minutes.

acts.name: Collect the first annual statements and disclosures of interests
steps: Each director, principal officer and member of a committee with Board-delegated powers signs the Article VI statement; each officer, director and key employee makes the Article IX disclosure; the Secretary keeps them (Article VI, Article IX).

acts.name: The Board of Directors adopts the Whistleblower Policy
acts.threshold: the act of a majority of Directors present at a meeting at which a quorum is present (Bylaws 4.10), or written action under Bylaws 4.12
preconditions: A quorum under Bylaws 4.10, or written action under Bylaws 4.12.
The Board either establishes the Finance and Audit Committee and appoints its chair (Bylaws 6.1, 6.3), or accepts that reports go to the Chair of the Board until it does.
steps: Adopt policies/drafts/whistleblower.md by the vote stated and record the adoption in the minutes.

acts.name: The Board of Directors adopts the Document Retention and Destruction Policy
acts.threshold: the act of a majority of Directors present at a meeting at which a quorum is present (Bylaws 4.10), or written action under Bylaws 4.12
preconditions: A quorum under Bylaws 4.10, or written action under Bylaws 4.12.
The Board adopts a period for each record class the schedule lists as unstated, or accepts that those classes are kept until it does.
steps: Adopt policies/drafts/document-retention.md by the vote stated and record the adoption in the minutes.

acts.name: Publish the adopted policies in UOR-Foundation/.github
preconditions: The text published is the text adopted, as the minutes record it.
steps: Open a pull request in UOR-Foundation/.github under its standard workflow adding governance/conflict-of-interest-policy.md, governance/whistleblower-policy.md and governance/document-retention-and-destruction-policy.md, each with its adoption date.
After it merges, pin the new commit in nonprofit/sources.json and re-project nonprofit/register.json, whose Part VI lines 12a, 13 and 14 then find the published policies.
